newsitem.title: USA: Denver officials relieved by SEC decision in probe.
newsitem.headline: Denver officials relieved by SEC decision in probe.

text.p: Denver officials on Friday expressed relief and gratitude that the city had been cleared of charges in the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission's probe of Denver International Airport bonds.
"We're quite pleased. It was the right decision," said Dan Muse, attorney for the city and county of Denver.
Muse held a press conference with 18 other officials representing the city, the airport and other groups.
Tom Boyle, an attorney who represented the city, said he would not speculate about why Denver had been cleared other than to say he believed the SEC found no wrongdoing.
Another attorney for the city, Raymond Friedlob, said he expected an SEC "pay-to-play" probe to be dropped.
Earlier on Friday, Denver officials said the SEC has notified the city it has been cleared of charges in the commission's probe of the airport's bonds.
But SEC staff said it has not ended a "pay-to-play" probe of underwritings involving the city.
The staff is examining whether or not two securities firms won top slots in the city's bond underwriting group in the early 1990s in return for political contributions to the city's mayor.
